summary: The note describes the Chief Justice of India and the constitutional rules on removing that office holder. It states that Article 124(4) of the Constitution of India sets out the removal procedure for a Supreme Court judge, and that this procedure also applies to the Chief Justice. It adds that the Chief Justice holds office until age 65 and can be removed only by impeachment by Parliament. The note is brief and ends before listing the impeachment steps.
one_line: Overview of the Chief Justice of India's tenure until age 65 and the impeachment-only removal process under Article 124(4).
key_facts: Article 124(4) of the Constitution of India lays down the procedure for removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court.
The procedure in Article 124(4) is applicable to the Chief Justice of India as well.
Once appointed, the Chief Justice of India remains in office until the age of 65 years.
The Chief Justice of India can be removed only through a process of impeachment by Parliament.
The note introduces the impeachment process as a list of steps but does not list them in the excerpt provided.
